newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe to cut costs, aims for profits.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe to cut costs, aims for profits.

text.p: CompuServe Corp said that its number one priority is to stabilize its earnings and return to profitability, as it continues to cut its costs and realign its business structure.
Earlier, CompuServe reported a third quarter loss of $14.2 million, or $0.15 a share, in line with analysts' expectations for a loss of $0.16 a share, according to First Call.

"While our third-quarter results show improvement over the second quarter, they are clearly not good enough," said Frank Salizzoni, chairman and acting CEO. Salizzoni is acting as CEO while the company looks to replace Robert Massey, who resigned.
Massey resigned on Monday and the company has hired an executive search firm as it looks both inside and outside the company to find a new chief executive officer.

CompuServe said that its flagship CSi online service saw its subscribers down at the end of the quarter by 100,000 to 2.8 million, from 2.9 million at the end of the second quarter, with the decline coming from the U.S. Its U.S. subscribers dropped 140,000 to 1.6 million, versus 1.7 million at the end of second quarter. European subscribers grew to 873,000, up 54,000 from 819,000 in the second quarter. Subscribers from
Previously, other overseas areas had 379,000 subscribers.
CompuServe also said that its Internet-only access service, Sprynet, grew to 270,000 members, up from 218,000 in the second quarter.

Its Japanese licensee, Nifty, grew to 2.17 million, from from 2.02 million in the second quarter. Including Nifty, CompuServe's total subscribers remained flat at 5,341,000 in the third quarter, from 5,341,000 in the second quarter.
Monthly revenue per subscriber improved in the third quarter to $15.22, compared with $15.06 in the second quarter and $14.48 in the first quarter.
The online service also said that it will continue to invest in its commercial networking business, which has been a successful source of growth for CompuServe.

CompuServe also said it will expand its network services offerings. In the third quarter, Network Services added 90 corporate customers, compared with 52 in the second quarter. CompuServe now has 1,151 customers for outsourced data communications, intranet solutions and applications hosting.
The company said it will continue to refocus its flagship CSi service on business, technical and professional users in North America, investing only in profitable growth areas.
Network Services revenues grew 27 percent to $65.2 million over the same period a year ago, representing 31 percent of total revenues of $211 million in the third quarter.
Overall third quarter revenues declined versus the second quarter, as CompuServe streamlined North American marketing programs to target business, professional and technical users.

Members for the combined CSi online service and Sprynet totalled 3,162,000 in the third quarter, down from 3,312,000 in the second quarter. CompuServe's exit from The Wow! service accounted for 102,000 of the 150,000 decline in subscribers. Wow! was its flat-rate service for consumers and families.
